name: Pagination
summary: Use pagination to help users move through a collection split across several pages.
whenToUse: Use when a long result set or collection is meaningfully divided into pages.
Use block-style previous and next links for content pages where destination labels help orientation.
whenNotToUse: Do not paginate a short list that is easier to scan on one page.
Do not use pagination to represent steps in a transaction.

anatomy.name: Pagination navigation
anatomy.description: A nav landmark has a concise pagination label.

anatomy.name: Previous and next links
anatomy.description: Directional links use rel=prev or rel=next and hidden “page” context.

anatomy.name: Page list
anatomy.description: Numbered links include accessible page labels and identify the current page.

variants.name: Numbered
variants.use: A results collection where users may move to a particular page.

variants.name: Block previous and next
variants.use: Sequential content where descriptive previous and next labels help users.

behaviour: Every destination is a normal server-resolvable link; no GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.
Omit previous on the first page and next on the last page instead of rendering disabled links.
Preserve active filters and sorting in pagination URLs.
accessibility: Set aria-current="page" on the current page link.
Give numbered links accessible names such as “Page 3”; hidden context distinguishes Previous page and Next page.
Hide decorative arrow SVGs using aria-hidden and focusable=false.
content: For block navigation, add a concise label that names the destination content.
Do not show every page number when a large range would become difficult to scan.
